result.summary:
Independently re-read docs/agents/design/REQ-040-schema.md in full (386 lines) rather than trusting DATA-DESIGNER's rework summary, and separately grepped the whole document for code fences (```) and executable-syntax markers (pgTable, UPDATE/DELETE/SELECT/CREATE TABLE, .references(), .notNull(), .defaultNow(), .defaultRandom(), export const). Zero code fences remain anywhere in the file. The five grep hits that remain (lines 24, 79, 175-176, 347) are all single-token inline-backtick references inside prose sentences describing the pattern in words (e.g. 'the actual pgTable(...) definition', 'CREATE TABLE invite_list_entries (...)' used as a plain-English description of what drizzle-kit generate will emit) -- none is a code block, none is copy-pasteable, none leaves BACKEND-DEV with nothing to write. This satisfies Step 1b check (d).

Precision check: Sec1's Column|Type|Nullable|Default|FK table (lines 54-66) is untouched and remains the authoritative, complete spec -- every column's type, nullability, default, and FK target/cascade behavior (all ON DELETE RESTRICT) is stated explicitly, including the one nullable FK (invite_code_id) and the two required self-referencing-to-users FKs (user_id, added_by) correctly distinguished. The new Sec1 'Reference shape' paragraph (lines 68-79) restates the identical shape in prose with no loss of information: PK default, all four FKs named with their targets and required/nullable status, the opened_at nullable timestamp, the three text columns with correct required/optional split, the created_at/updated_at pair, and the named uq_invite_list_entries_event_user unique index on (event_id, user_id) -- all present. Sec4.2's rewritten relink prose (lines 252-266) still states the exact two-step logic precisely enough to implement without judgment calls: step 1 is a conditional repoint of every A-row to B, gated on non-existence of a same-event B-row (the NOT EXISTS guard, described in words); step 2 deletes exactly the rows step 1's condition skipped; both run in one transaction, atomicity stated explicitly. This is traceable one-to-one against the original SQL version already verified correct in the prior step-01b pass -- no logic was lost or altered in the conversion, only the syntax form changed.

No-decision-changed check: Sec2's UNIQUE(event_id, user_id) (non-partial, same reasoning, same precedent tables cited) is byte-identical in substance to the version already confirmed. Sec3's hard-DELETE decision (audit_log.entity_id carries no FK, confirmed again by the same schema.ts citation) is identical. Sec1.3's business-card-field placement on invite_list_entries rather than profiles (three-point data-shape argument) is identical. Sec8's AC-closure table and Sec9's open-questions list are both unchanged from the version already verified to leave no AC unaddressed and no TBD/deferral language.

Token check (c) is N/A for this artefact: REQ-040-schema.md is a pure database schema design with no UI/visual surface -- it references no color, spacing, or typography tokens, so there is nothing in docs/Design system for AI agents/tokens/tokens.css for it to violate. This matches the established precedent for prior schema artefacts (REQ-031-schema.md, REQ-032-schema.md), neither of which references design tokens either.

All four Step 1b checks (a-d) pass. FAIL immediately on any single failure did not trigger -- no failures found.
